outcome: No result bearing on the Demazure conjecture is dated inside the window (26 January 2024 to 11 October 2026): its only mathematical results are pre-window, namely Lakshmibai, Musili and Seshadri's 1979 proof for classical groups and Littelmann's reported 1998 extension to all reductive groups, while the one in-window change to its Wikipedia article is a 4 October 2026 'citation needed' tag on the Littelmann sentence.
problem_asks: The bullet asks one thing: whether a conjecture about representations of algebraic groups over the integers holds. Parts: (a) the object is algebraic groups G over Z and their representations over Z (the bullet names no particular class of groups; the 1974 source is not readable to me, so whether the intended class is reductive groups is unconfirmed); (b) the claim is the conjecture as made by Demazure in 1974, which Wikipedia describes only as 'a conjecture about representations of algebraic groups over the integers' whose truth would extend many results of his paper from complex algebraic groups to algebraic groups over fields of other characteristics or over the integers; (c) on Grokipedia's paraphrase (unverified against the 1974 text), for each dominant weight lambda and Weyl group element tau, the Z-submodule of the admissible Z-form generated by tau acting on a highest-weight vector is a direct summand of that Z-form. Part (b) gives two readings that may differ: a characteristic-free extension of the 1974 results, and the Z-form direct-summand statement in (c). Which of these the bullet asks for is left for the judging pass.

events.what_happened: Michel Demazure, 'Désingularisation des variétés de Schubert généralisées', Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4) 7 (1974), no. 1, 53–88, DOI 10.24033/asens.1261. The conjecture is posed here, on p. 83 according to Wikipedia and a search snippet. The numdam PDF was not readable to me, so I could not read the statement or whether any partial result accompanies it. This entry records the posing, not a result.
events.delivers: None. This is the posing of the conjecture. Per Wikipedia it is 'a conjecture about representations of algebraic groups over the integers', and its truth would extend many results of the paper from complex algebraic groups to other characteristics or to Z.
events.direction: Not a result. Poses the conjecture.

events.what_happened: V. Lakshmibai, C. Musili and C. S. Seshadri, 'Geometry of G/P' (announcement), Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.) 1 (1979), 432–435, DOI 10.1090/S0273-0979-1979-14631-7; the AMS page returned HTTP 403, so I did not read it. The full paper is 'Geometry of G/P-IV (Standard monomial theory for classical types)', Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. (Math. Sci.) 88 (1979), no. 4, 279–362, DOI 10.1007/BF02842481, whose IAS repository record lists the keyword 'Demazure's Conjecture' (record opened; abstract field reads 'This article does not have an abstract'). Wikipedia states that Seshadri's and their standard monomial theory work shows the conjecture for classical groups.
events.delivers: Per Wikipedia and the keyword record: the conjecture for classical groups, via standard monomial theory. Restriction: classical types only (Grokipedia says types A to D). Not established by my sources: the base ring or field, the characteristic, and whether the result is stated over Z at all. The standard monomial theory article says 'Standard monomial theory can be used to prove Demazure's conjecture' without a theorem reference.
events.remains: Non-classical reductive groups. Any Z-form content of the conjecture, if the bullet is read as the Z-form statement. Whether the classical case is fully closed here: a search snippet attributed to Brion and Lakshmibai (not opened) says the classical program is completed in 'Geometry of G/P-V', J. Algebra 100 (1986), which I did not check.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the Indian Academy of Sciences (Mathematical Sciences) and Bulletin of the AMS
checked_by.qualification: Journals of record that published the papers
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the papers. I did not find a referee report, a published review text, or a later verification of this result.

events.doubts: Scope: the classical result as described covers classical types only. The Bull. AMS note could not be read (403), and the full paper's abstract is absent from the record. The 1986 completion claim is a lead only and is unverified. No doubt about correctness was found in any source.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for classical groups, per Wikipedia and the keyword record. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Peter Littelmann, 'The path model, the quantum Frobenius map and standard monomial theory', in the proceedings Algebraic Groups and their Representations (listed as 1998; Grokipedia gives a 1997 Cambridge conference). Wikipedia says Littelmann extended the classical-groups result to all reductive algebraic groups; that sentence has no inline citation and was tagged 'citation needed' on 4 October 2026. Wikipedia's Standard monomial theory article says 'Littelmann (1998) proved their conjectures using the Littelmann path model' and cites this paper. A search snippet says Littelmann's Cambridge survey (cambridge.pdf) lists a proof of Demazure's conjecture among geometric applications; I could not open that file. The paper itself was not read.
events.delivers: Claimed in secondary sources only: the conjecture for all reductive algebraic groups. Not established by anything I read: the base ring or characteristic, or whether the result is a Z-form (direct-summand) statement as Grokipedia's paraphrase requires.
events.remains: Whether the Z-form statement in part (c) of problem_asks is covered. Whether the characteristic-free or integral content of part (b) is covered. The paper's exact theorem numbering.
events.doubts: The only sentence in Wikipedia carrying this claim has no citation and was tagged 'citation needed' on 4 October 2026 by AnomieBOT. Grokipedia dates the proof both to 'late 1990s' and to 1997 in different places. The earlier record in data/mark_2026-09-22 cites a different Littelmann paper, 'Cones, crystals, and patterns', for this extension; I could not confirm that (see the next event). I found no review or later paper discussing this extension in my searches.
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for all reductive groups, per secondary sources. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: P. Littelmann, 'Cones, crystals, and patterns', Transform. Groups 3 (1998), no. 2, 145–179, DOI 10.1007/BF01236431. The Springer page redirected to a login and I did not open it. Search snippets describe it as generalising Gelfand–Tsetlin patterns to complex semisimple groups via the path model and crystals, with a cone description of crystal points. No snippet mentions the Demazure conjecture.
events.revisions: A preprint titled 'Paths, cones and Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns' (1996) is named in a search snippet; not checked.
events.delivers: Not established to bear on the conjecture. From snippets it describes a cone and pattern parametrisation of crystals, not a Z-form or direct-summand statement, and not a proof of the Demazure conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as I can tell.
events.doubts: Discarded as a neighbour, with reason: it is cited in the earlier record for the reductive extension, and nothing I could read links it to the conjecture. I did not read the paper, so this is a reading of snippets, not of the text.
events.direction: Not stated in any source I read as bearing on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Correct proofs of Demazure's 1974 character formula for Demazure modules in arbitrary characteristic, by S. Andersen (1985) and by S. Ramanan and A. Ramanathan (1985), using Frobenius splitting (Mehta and Ramanathan also cited). The Demazure module Wikipedia page I opened says Victor Kac pointed out that Demazure's proof has a serious gap; the Andersen and Ramanan–Ramanathan credits come from search snippets of other pages, not from the page I opened. A later Ramanathan paper, 'Equations defining Schubert varieties and Frobenius splittings of diagonals', Publ. Math. IHES 65 (1987), appeared in search results; I did not read it.
events.delivers: A characteristic-free proof of Demazure's character formula, i.e. the character of a Demazure module or of global sections on a Schubert variety. This is a character formula, not the Z-form or direct-summand statement that Grokipedia gives. It is ambiguous whether the character formula is part of the conjecture: on Wikipedia's description (the conjecture extends the 1974 results to other characteristics), it plausibly is; on Grokipedia's, it is a neighbour.
events.remains: The Z-form statement in part (c) of problem_asks. Any integral claim.
events.doubts: Demazure's own proof of the 1974 formula had a gap pointed out by V. Kac (1983), per the Wikipedia Demazure module page. The Andersen and Ramanan–Ramanathan papers were not read, so the correctness of these repairs rests on secondary mentions.
events.direction: Confirms the arbitrary-characteristic character formula. No counterexample. Whether this is part of the Demazure conjecture is the scope question the judging pass has to settle.

events.what_happened: Littelmann conjectured in 1995 a crystal-basis version of Demazure's refined character formula (Wikipedia Demazure module page, citing 'Crystal graphs and Young tableaux', J. Algebra 175 (1995)); Kashiwara proved it. The Wikipedia page gives Kashiwara's proof as 1993, which predates the 1995 conjecture; the inconsistency is not resolved here.
events.delivers: Not the Demazure conjecture. This is a different conjecture, made by Littelmann about crystal bases, that shares the Demazure name because it concerns Demazure characters.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as this event goes.
events.direction: Not about the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Rekha Biswal, Ken Ono and Jujian Zhang, 'Chebyshev quotients, Demazure multiplicities, and Dyck-path models', arXiv:2604.25246, v1 28 April 2026, v2 19 May 2026. It studies Chebyshev quotients and Demazure flag multiplicities for sl2[t] fusion products, and proves positivity of their coefficients. Section 6 (appendix) describes AxiomProver, an Axiom Math system, being given Lean formalisation tasks for the paper's theorems, and says the theorems were produced and formalised in Lean/Mathlib from statements written by the authors. The paper does not mention a Demazure conjecture of 1974. This is a neighbour that shares a name, and it is an AI-linked event.
events.revisions: v1 28 Apr 2026; v2 19 May 2026 (per the arXiv abstract page as fetched).
events.delivers: Positivity of coefficients of Chebyshev quotients in several families, with Lean files for the theorems. A result on Demazure multiplicities (Demazure flags for fusion products), not on representations of algebraic groups over Z. Not an answer to any part of problem_asks.

checked_by.qualification: Machine check of the Lean files, not a human reading
checked_by.what_they_did: The paper reports that the Lean files for its theorems were accepted by the Lean type checker.

events.doubts: Discarded neighbour: a different problem. Not checked for sorry in the Lean files. disputes.summary: Who proved the extension to all reductive groups. Wikipedia credits Littelmann with no inline citation, tagged 'citation needed' on 4 October 2026. Grokipedia dates the proof to the late 1990s (also 1997 in another place) and cites Littelmann's path-model paper. The earlier record in data/mark_2026-09-22 attributes it to Littelmann's 'Cones, crystals, and patterns' (Transform. Groups 1998), which search snippets describe as a different subject. Not resolved here: the path-model paper and the Cones paper were not read.

What the conjecture asserts. Wikipedia describes it only as a conjecture about representations over the integers that would extend the 1974 results to other characteristics or to Z. Grokipedia gives a Z-form direct-summand statement, which I could not check against Demazure's 1974 text. On the first reading the arbitrary-characteristic character formula (Andersen 1985; Ramanan and Ramanathan 1985) may fall inside the conjecture, and Demazure's 1974 proof of that formula had a gap (Kac, 1983). On the second reading it does not.

summary: Nothing bearing on the conjecture was found in the window. Its status rests on two pre-window claims, and the sources disagree about what the conjecture says. Demazure posed it in 1974 (Annales ENS 7, p. 83 per Wikipedia), but I could not read the 1974 paper: the numdam PDF returned binary. Wikipedia gives no formal statement; Grokipedia, which I opened as a secondary source, paraphrases a Z-form direct-summand claim (for dominant λ and Weyl element τ, the Z-submodule of an admissible Z-form generated by τ acting on a highest-weight vector is a direct summand). That is the only formal statement I have, and I could not confirm it. Wikipedia credits Lakshmibai, Musili and Seshadri (1979; the Bull. AMS note and 'Geometry of G/P-IV', whose IAS keyword record includes 'Demazure's Conjecture') with the classical-groups case via standard monomial theory, and says Littelmann extended it to all reductive groups. The Littelmann sentence has no citation and was tagged 'citation needed' on 4 October 2026, with an unexplained 32-byte removal the same day by another editor; the article's content was otherwise unchanged from 2021 to that date, so no in-window content change to the status was found. The reductive extension is attributed to 'The path model, the quantum Frobenius map and standard monomial theory' (1998 proceedings, 1997 conference per Grokipedia). I could not read it. A search snippet says Littelmann's survey lists a proof of Demazure's conjecture among its geometric applications; I could not verify it. The earlier record attributes the extension to 'Cones, crystals, and patterns'; the snippets describe that paper as about cones and patterns for crystals, so I record it as a discarded neighbour. Close calls: (1) Scope over Z. Standard monomial theory and the path model are, as described, over fields of any characteristic, not over Z, and I found no source saying these results address Z-forms. Whether they settle a Z statement is for the judging pass. (2) Which conjecture. If the bullet is the characteristic-free extension of the 1974 results, the 1985 character-formula proofs are inside it, and the status is 'settled in 1985 at the latest'. If it is the Z-form direct-summand statement, they are neighbours. (3) Name collisions. Many 2024–2026 arXiv papers use 'Demazure' for modules, crystals, operators or products; none I checked cites or restates this conjecture, so none is recorded as an event. AI: no source names an AI system for this conjecture, and none of the searches found an AI claim about it. The only AI-linked item found is AxiomProver's formalisation in Biswal, Ono and Zhang (2026), a paper on Demazure multiplicities that does not mention the conjecture; it is recorded as a discarded neighbour with the authors' own sentence. The AI search used lab, tracker and Lean terms; the Quanta, Epoch and Tao results were off-target snippets that I did not open.
competing_reading: The conjecture was settled in 1979 for classical groups and in 1998 for all reductive groups, so the status is 'resolved decades ago', and nothing in the window changes that. On this reading the 1998 Littelmann event is the settling event, and the missing citation is a Wikipedia housekeeping issue. The opposite reading: the bullet names integral representations, and every settling result I found is stated over fields rather than over Z, so the Z-form statement may never have been addressed and the bullet would remain open. A third reading is that the bullet is the characteristic-free extension, in which case the 1985 proofs of the character formula are what settled it.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Demazure 1974, p. 83: the exact statement, to decide between the Z-form direct-summand reading and the characteristic-free reading. (b) Littelmann's 1998 'The path model, the quantum Frobenius map and standard monomial theory': whether it proves the reductive claim, over what base or characteristic, and whether it covers Z-forms. (c) Lakshmibai, Musili and Seshadri 1979: the main theorem and its base ring, and whether G/P-V (J. Algebra 1986) is the completion of the classical case. (d) Littelmann's Cambridge survey (cambridge.pdf): whether 'Demazure's conjecture' is listed with a theorem reference. (e) The 4 October 2026 Wikipedia diff, to see which sentence the 'citation needed' tag was placed on, and whether the Barçaforlife edit touched the status text.

(2) Littelmann's 1998 proceedings paper and his Cambridge survey were not readable (binary PDF), so the all-reductive claim and its base ring or characteristic are unverified, and the 'Demazure's conjecture' application listed in the survey is from a snippet. events.credibility_reason: The claim rests on secondary sources only: the Wikipedia sentence is uncited and tagged 'citation needed', the paper and survey were unread, and whether the result is stated over Z (as the statement requires) rather than over fields is unconfirmed.

events.ai_basis: AxiomProver’s role was to convert these statements into Lean and to construct machine-checkable formal proofs.

judgement.why: Every result bearing on the conjecture is pre-snapshot. LMS 1979 settles the classical-groups restriction and was published in a journal of record, so case/digested. Littelmann's reported extension to all reductive groups would answer the whole statement, but nobody in the record read it, the only attribution is an uncited Wikipedia sentence, and the integral (over Z) content is unconfirmed; I mark it whole/unreviewed/doubtful rather than resolved. The 1985 character-formula proofs are over fields of arbitrary characteristic and concern Demazure's character formula, not the integral-representation statement the bullet names, so variant (close call: on Wikipedia's looser description they might be inside it). The 2026 Biswal–Ono–Zhang paper is about Demazure multiplicities for sl2[t] fusion products, a different question, so variant; AxiomProver constructed the proofs of the paper's theorems from author-supplied statements, which is generated for that event alone, though it is discarded as a variant.
judgement.doubts: The exact 1974 statement was never read; the Z-form reading rests on Grokipedia. If Littelmann's 1998 paper were confirmed to prove the integral statement and counted as digested by its proceedings publication, the problem would be open_stale rather than open. The Littelmann attribution itself is disputed (path-model paper vs 'Cones, crystals, and patterns').
